correctness.rationale: The CRT class has residues 1 or 2 at each prime below h. Prime endpoint P=h+1 protects all residue-1 coordinates; exclusion of primes dividing h+2 protects all residue-2 coordinates. Every composite or small-prime interior m=i+1 is killed by an untouched prime <=\(h/2\); every large prime in T survives since other selected primes >\(h/2\) cannot divide the even number m+1<=h. Nonselected large primes are killed at their own coordinate. Distinct T yield distinct classes. PNT makes |U_h| unbounded, giving each atom positive mass and hence \(c_{r+1}-c_r>0\). Standard-library checker independently verified 4,042 CRT patterns and five exhaustive histograms; checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The recently introduced constants \(c_r\) are cumulative multiplicity weights for rough integers in a prime gap. Whether any exact multiplicity is forbidden matters: positivity of \(c_r\) and even \(c_r\) asymptotics allow flat adjacent constants. The binomial full-support result provides a structural mechanism at a natural infinite family of prime-predecessor gap lengths, ruling out every missing exact-multiplicity layer. It yields positivity of the conditional exact-count leading coefficient for every fixed r, not just isolated numerical evidence.
